title_en: Ma Shuifa v. Shaanxi Heavy-Duty Automobile Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over right to health
ruling_gist_en: A producer shall bear the burden of proof for its statutory grounds for exemption from liability. A product quality inspection certificate issued by the producer itself cannot constitute a statutory ground for exemption from liability. If the producer fails to provide evidence proving that its product conforms to quality standards, it shall bear tort liability for compensation to the victim.

full_text_en:
Ma Shuifa v. Shaanxi Heavy Duty Automobile Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over right to health

[Ruling Summary]

The producer shall bear the burden of proof for its statutory exemptions; its self-issued product quality inspection certificate cannot constitute a statutory exemption. If the producer fails to provide evidence proving that its product meets the quality standards, it shall bear tort liability for compensation to the victim.

Plaintiff: Ma Shuifa, male, 23 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yanling County, Henan Province.

Defendant: Wang Gang, male, 45 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Suzhou City, Anhui Province.

Defendant: Xiao County Hong'an Automobile Transportation Co., Ltd., domiciled at Yezhuang Village, Dulou Town, Xiao County, Anhui Province.
Legal Representative: Tao Hui, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Shaanxi Heavy Duty Automobile Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jingwei Industrial Park, Economic and Technological Development Zone, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Tan Xuguang, Chairman of the company.

The plaintiff, Ma Shuifa, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City against the defendants Wang Gang, Xiao County Hong'an Automobile Transportation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong'an Company), and Shaanxi Heavy Duty Automobile Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanxi Heavy Truck Company) regarding a dispute over the right to health.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff alleged that on July 15, 2013, the defendant Wang Gang drove a heavy-duty dump truck (license plate number Anhui L60932, owner: Hong'an Company, manufacturer: Shanxi Heavy Truck Company; hereinafter referred to as the vehicle involved) to the "Xuchang Drive Shaft Factory Southeast Repair Station" located at Qilin Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, which the plaintiff operated, for repair due to a water tank malfunction. During the repair process, the base of the cab lifting cylinder suddenly fractured, causing the cab to collapse and crush the plaintiff. After being injured, the plaintiff was sent to the hospital for treatment. As of August 1, 2013, medical expenses totaled RMB 86,007.6. The plaintiff now requests that the three defendants jointly compensate the plaintiff and bear joint and several liability among themselves.

Defendants' Defenses:

Defendant Wang Gang and Hong'an Company argued: 1. The vehicle involved is indeed owned by Hong'an Company, but the company performed normal maintenance and annual inspections on the vehicle; 2. The vehicle was sent to the repair station where the plaintiff worked for repairs, establishing a repair contract relationship between the parties. The accident occurred during the repair period, and the defendants were not at fault; 3. The cab collapse was caused by the plaintiff's own improper operation, unrelated to the defendants. Therefore, the defendants have no connection to the accident, and the court should reject the plaintiff's claim for joint and several liability.

Defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company argued: 1. The vehicle involved was indeed manufactured by the company, but it passed quality inspection upon leaving the factory; 2. The vehicle involved had been in use for more than three years and was long past its warranty period; 3. The plaintiff allegedly violated operating procedures when lifting the cab during repair and failed to lift it to the correct position, which caused the plaintiff's injury; 4. The losses incurred by the plaintiff should be borne by his employer. Therefore, the court should reject the plaintiff's claim for joint and several liability.

Facts Found by the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City at First Instance:

On July 15, 2013, the defendant Wang Gang drove the vehicle involved to the "Xuchang Drive Shaft Factory Southeast Repair Station" located at Qilin Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing City, for water tank repair. Because the water tank was located under the cab, the repair station's mechanic, the plaintiff Ma Shuifa, lifted the cab and was working under the cab to repair the water tank when the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly of the vehicle's cab suddenly fractured, causing the cab to fall and crush him. Ma Shuifa was hospitalized at the 81st Hospital of the People's Liberation Army for 17 days and was diagnosed with traumatic paraplegia and a burst fracture of the L1 vertebra. As of August 1, 2013, medical expenses totaled RMB 89,989.6 (of which the medical expense receipts issued and claimed by Ma Shuifa amounted to RMB 86,007.6, and the defendant Wang Gang additionally provided medical expense receipts totaling RMB 3,982).

It was further found that the manufacturer of the vehicle involved was the defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company, and the vehicle was purchased by the defendant Hong'an Company on September 18, 2010. At the time of the accident, the vehicle had undergone normal annual inspection and obtained a road transport permit. The driver of the vehicle involved, the defendant Wang Gang, held a B2 driver's license and had a road cargo transport driver qualification. The vehicle involved had not been modified since purchase.

It was also found that on July 17, 2013, the Qilin Police Station received a report from the defendant Wang Gang that a repairman working on his vehicle was injured by the falling cab and had been sent to the hospital. The police recorded this report. No other police reports related to the accident were filed. On July 31, 2013, the plaintiff Ma Shuifa filed the lawsuit.

During the first-instance trial, the defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company argued that the fractured component—the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly—was indeed an original part, but the entire vehicle and its parts had passed quality inspection before leaving the factory and complied with national standards. The reason the cab fell backward and crushed the plaintiff Ma Shuifa was that the plaintiff did not lift the cab to the correct position, so the defendant should bear no liability. Ma Shuifa argued that he had lifted the cab to the proper position following correct operating procedures, and the cause of his injury was a quality defect in the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly manufactured by Shanxi Heavy Truck Company, which suddenly fractured.

Opinion of the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City at First Instance:

A citizen's right to life and health is protected by law. In this case, the injury suffered by the plaintiff Ma Shuifa was caused by the cab tilting backward after the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly of the vehicle involved fractured. The parties had no dispute on this fact, and the court confirmed it. The focus of the dispute was the cause of the fracture of the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly. The defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company should bear the burden of proving that the vehicle and parts it manufactured were qualified products. However, the evidence it provided, such as the vehicle inspection certificate and the physical and chemical inspection report of the parts, were all self-issued internally by Shanxi Heavy Truck Company. Moreover, after the court's clarification, Shanxi Heavy Truck Company did not apply for a judicial appraisal of the cause of the fracture of the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly. Therefore, it should be presumed that the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly had a product quality defect. There was a causal relationship between the plaintiff's injury and the product quality defect in the vehicle manufactured by Shanxi Heavy Truck Company. Accordingly, Shanxi Heavy Truck Company should bear civil liability for Ma Shuifa's injury.

Parties have the responsibility to provide evidence to support their claims. The defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company argued that the plaintiff Ma Shuifa violated operating procedures during the repair and failed to lift the cab to the correct position, but it failed to provide evidence proving this. Moreover, it could not reasonably explain whether there was a necessary causal relationship between the part fracture and the failure to lift the cab to the correct position. Therefore, the court did not accept this defense argument. The right to claim compensation for damage caused by product defects is extinguished ten years after the defective product causing the damage is delivered to the initial consumer, unless the product has an express safety use period that has not yet expired. The court did not accept Shanxi Heavy Truck Company's argument that the vehicle involved was purchased in 2010 and had passed the two-year warranty period, so it should not bear liability. As for Shanxi Heavy Truck Company's argument that the RMB 240 expense for multiple hepatitis B and C tests in the medical expense receipts provided by Ma Shuifa was unnecessary and should be deducted, this was inconsistent with the facts and law, and the court did not accept it either.

The defendants Wang Gang and Hong'an Company sent the vehicle involved, which had a water tank malfunction, to the "Xuchang Drive Shaft Factory Southeast Repair Station" for repair, forming a de facto contractual relationship for work. If a contractor causes damage to a third party or to itself during the completion of the work, the hiring party is not liable for compensation. Therefore, the plaintiff Ma Shuifa's request for Wang Gang and Hong'an Company to bear joint and several liability for compensation for his injury losses was legally unfounded, and the court did not support it.

In summary, based on the facts found in this case, the defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company should bear full responsibility for the plaintiff Ma Shuifa's economic losses after the injury. The court supported Ma Shuifa's claim for compensation of medical expenses of RMB 86,007.6 (as of August 1, 2013). Regarding the additional medical expense receipts of RMB 3,982 provided by the defendant Wang Gang and the RMB 7,000 Wang Gang voluntarily paid to Ma Shuifa, since the plaintiff did not amend his claim accordingly and Wang Gang did not assert these amounts during the trial, the court did not address them.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 15, 16, 26, and 41 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, Article 45(2) of the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City rendered the following judgment on October 29, 2013:

1. The defendant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company shall compensate the plaintiff Ma Shuifa for post-injury medical expenses of RMB 86,007.6 (as of August 1, 2013), to be paid in full within 10 days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective.
2. The other claims of the plaintiff Ma Shuifa are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Shanxi Heavy Truck Company appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, arguing:

(1) Regarding the fact of Ma Shuifa's injury, Ma Shuifa did not provide sufficient evidence, and the facts found by the first-instance court lacked a basis.
(2) Ma Shuifa was not the owner of the "Xuchang Drive Shaft Factory Southeast Repair Station"; the actual owner was Wang Changling. The appellant requested the first-instance court to add Wang Changling as a joint defendant, but the first-instance judgment did not address this.
(3) Ma Shuifa himself was grossly negligent in causing the damage. He did not lift the cab to the proper position, violated the professional standards expected of an automobile repairman, and intentionally worked under the cab in violation of regulations. Therefore, the appellant should not bear full liability for compensation for his injury.
(4) The cause of action in this case is a dispute over the right to health. The first-instance court violated legal provisions by requiring the appellant to prove that the vehicle had no defects. Moreover, the vehicle certificate provided by the appellant and the fact that the vehicle passed annual inspections each year fully proved that the vehicle involved was qualified.
(5) The first-instance court's finding that Wang Gang and Hong'an Company should not bear joint and several liability was erroneous in fact and law.
(6) This case involves multiple defendants with significant disputes. The first-instance court's use of summary procedure with a single acting judge constituted a procedural violation.

The appellee Ma Shuifa responded: The first-instance court's findings of fact were clear, and the judgment was correct. The appellee requests the second-instance court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The appellees Wang Gang and Hong'an Company responded: They have no objection to the first-instance judgment.

None of the parties presented new evidence, facts, or reasons during the second instance.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, after the second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

Opinion of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court at Second Instance:

The issues in dispute in this second instance are:

1. Whether the first-instance court had sufficient factual basis to find that the cab of the vehicle involved fell backward and crushed the appellee Ma Shuifa;
2. Whether the first-instance court's finding that the vehicle involved had a product quality defect complied with the law;
3. Whether the first-instance court correctly determined liability;
4. Whether the first-instance court's trial procedure was lawful.

(1) Regarding whether the first-instance court had sufficient factual basis to find that the cab of the vehicle involved fell backward and crushed the appellee Ma Shuifa:

After the accident, the appellee Wang Gang immediately sent Ma Shuifa to the hospital for treatment and advanced part of the medical expenses. Wang Gang had no objection to the fact that Ma Shuifa was crushed by the cab of the vehicle involved falling backward. Furthermore, according to the "Explanation on the Vehicle Fault Situation" submitted by the appellant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company in the first instance, it stated that while Ma Shuifa was disassembling the intercooler, the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly of the cab suddenly fractured, causing the cab to fall backward and crush him. Therefore, the first-instance court's finding that the cab fell backward and crushed Ma Shuifa had sufficient factual basis. The court did not accept Shanxi Heavy Truck Company's appeal argument that the first-instance court lacked sufficient factual basis for finding Ma Shuifa's injury.

(2) Regarding whether the first-instance court's finding that the vehicle involved had a product quality defect complied with the law:

Based on the facts found, while the appellee Ma Shuifa was repairing the water tank of the vehicle involved, the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly of the vehicle's cab suddenly fractured, causing the cab to fall and crush Ma Shuifa. Article 46 of the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a product defect means that the product poses an unreasonable risk to the safety of persons or property other than itself; where there are national or industry standards for ensuring human health and the safety of persons and property, a defect means non-compliance with such standards. The court held that national and industry standards are the minimum standards that a product should meet, and a product that meets the "standards" may still have an unreasonable risk. In this case, the sudden fracture of the lifting cylinder axle seat bracket assembly caused the cab to fall and injure Ma Shuifa. The appellant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company argued that the vehicle was a qualified product with no defect. Therefore, it should provide evidence of the cause of the part fracture to prove that the fracture was not caused by an inherent defect in the product or other reasons. However, Shanxi Heavy Truck Company refused to provide evidence and apply for appraisal on the cause of the part fracture, arguing that Ma Shuifa should bear the burden of proof for the cause of the fracture. Consequently, Shanxi Heavy Truck Company should bear the legal consequences of failing to meet its burden of proof. The first-instance court's finding that the part fracture constituted a product defect had factual and legal basis, and this court supported it.

(3) Regarding whether the first-instance court correctly determined liability:

Article 41 of the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where personal injury or damage to property other than the defective product itself is caused by a product defect, the producer shall bear liability for compensation. The producer shall not bear liability for compensation if it can prove any of the following circumstances: (1) the product was not put into circulation; (2) the defect causing the damage did not exist when the product was put into circulation; or (3) the existence of the defect could not be discovered given the state of science and technology at the time the product was put into circulation. Based on the facts found by the court, Shanxi Heavy Truck Company failed to provide evidence proving the existence of any circumstance under which the producer would not bear liability. Article 41 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a product defect causes damage to another person, the producer shall bear tort liability. Product liability is a no-fault liability for the producer. The appellee Ma Shuifa was injured due to a product defect in the vehicle involved. Pursuant to the above legal provisions, the appellant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company shall bear full liability for compensation for the losses Ma Shuifa sustained from this injury. Shanxi Heavy Truck Company's argument that the appellees Wang Gang and Hong'an Company should bear joint and several liability and that Ma Shuifa should bear partial liability lacked legal basis, and the court did not support it.

(4) Regarding whether the first-instance court's trial procedure was lawful:

Article 132 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a party who must participate in the litigation jointly has not participated, the people's court shall notify them to participate. In this case, the appellee Ma Shuifa claimed compensation from Shanxi Heavy Truck Company, Wang Gang, and Hong'an Company based on damage caused by a product defect. Wang Changling was not a necessary joint participant in this litigation. The first-instance court's failure to add Wang Changling as a joint defendant complied with the law. Article 133(3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the people's court shall, based on the circumstances of the case, determine whether to apply summary procedure or ordinary procedure for the cases it accepts. The appellant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company's claim that the use of summary procedure in the first instance was unlawful lacked sufficient basis, and the court did not support it.

In conclusion, the first-instance court's findings of fact were clear, and the judgment rendered was proper and should be affirmed. The appellant Shanxi Heavy Truck Company's appeal lacked sufficient evidence and sufficient reasoning. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 170(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 16, 2014:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
